meta.description: Credited to the 14th Dalai Lama and squarely in line with his teaching — but the 1984 book named as its source is lending-restricted, so the wording is unpinned.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'My true religion is Kindness'?
meta.ogDescription: Wikiquote sources it to Kindness, Clarity, and Insight (1984). No page, and we could not open the book — so we say attributed, not verified.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.authorDates: born 6 July 1935 · Tenzin Gyatso, 14th Dalai Lama; Tibetan Buddhist spiritual leader
answer.sourceLine: Wikiquote lists this sentence in its main sourced section for the 14th Dalai Lama and gives the source as Kindness, Clarity, and Insight (1984), the Snow Lion collection translated and edited by Jeffrey Hopkins and Elizabeth Napper. It gives no page, and the Internet Archive's scan is lending-restricted, so we could not open the book to confirm the wording — which is why this page says attributed rather than verified. The sentiment is documented all over his work; this exact sentence is not pinned to a page.

trail: Wikiquote’s page for the 14th Dalai Lama ↗ carries “My true religion is Kindness.” in its main Quotes section — not under Misattributed or Disputed — and sources it to Kindness, Clarity, and Insight (1984). No page number is given.

We confirmed the book exists exactly as named: the Internet Archive’s catalogue record ↗ gives Kindness, clarity, and insight, 1984, Snow Lion Publications, Ithaca, with Jeffrey Hopkins and Elizabeth Napper as translators and editors. We could not read inside it — the item is lending-restricted and the full text returns an authorisation error — so we are not claiming to have seen the sentence on a page.
Quote Investigator has published no investigation of this line, so there is no specialist finding to defer to here. That is our own search result, not a claim we can cite.
The Dalai Lama’s date of birth, 6 July 1935, and the 1989 Nobel Peace Prize are confirmed against his Wikipedia entry ↗.
source.excerptNote: Wikiquote records a longer variant immediately beside it — “My religion is very simple. My religion is kindness.” — which it traces to Tibet, a Guide to the Land of Fascination (1988) by Trilok Chandra Majupuria and Indra Majupuria. That is the form most often seen in circulation.
source.rightsHolder: His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama and his publishers
source.rightsNote: This is a living author’s twentieth-century writing, so it is in copyright wherever it was first printed. The book named as its source, Kindness, Clarity, and Insight, was published in 1984 by Snow Lion Publications — half a century after the 1931 United States public-domain cut-off. Quote & cite it, but do not treat it as free to reuse.

author.bio: His Holiness Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama, was born to a farming family in Amdo in 1935 and recognised as the Dalai Lama as a small child. He has lived in exile in India since 1959, and spent the following decades arguing a consistent case: that compassion is not a religious ornament but a practical requirement for human societies, and that it can be cultivated with or without religion. He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The appeal of the line is that it refuses the question it is asked. Invited to name his religion, the most recognisable Buddhist alive answers with a behaviour rather than a creed — something a Christian, an atheist or a Jain could adopt without changing anything else they believe.

That is a position he has argued consistently rather than a stray aphorism, which is exactly why the wording is so hard to pin: he has said versions of it for decades, in several languages and dozens of books, and the compilers who quote it rarely say which one they took it from.
context.pull: Invited to name his religion, he answers with a behaviour rather than a creed.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote carries "My true religion is Kindness." in its main sourced Quotes section for the 14th Dalai Lama and gives the source as Kindness, Clarity, and Insight (1984), with no page number.
Wikiquote records the variant "My religion is very simple. My religion is kindness." as quoted in Tibet, a Guide to the Land of Fascination (1988) by Trilok Chandra Majupuria and Indra Majupuria.

The Internet Archive holds a catalogue record for Kindness, clarity, and insight, 1984, Snow Lion Publications, Ithaca, by the 14th Dalai Lama with Jeffrey Hopkins and Elizabeth Napper. The item is access-restricted and its full text is not readable.
The Internet Archive holds a 1990 Snow Lion anthology, The Dalai Lama, a policy of kindness, edited by Sidney Piburn.
The 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, was born 6 July 1935 and received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989.
